To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adipose Rab10 is essential for insulin-stimulate glucose uptake and GLUT 4 translocation in adipocytes.

adipose Rab10 KO mice have impaired insulin-stimulated adipose glucose uptake, and that the impact of impaired adipose insulin sensitivity on glucose homeostasis results from a near complete failure in the suppression of hepatic gluconeogenesis by insulin rather than a significant impairment in muscle glucose uptake or suppression of plasma free-fatty acids.

disruption of adipose Rab10-dependent insulin signaling causes hepatic insulin resistance, but not muscle insulin resistance, in female mice, and that this hepatic insulin resistance is driven by the near complete failure of adipose insulin signaling to suppress hepatic gluconeogenesis rather than by a significant inhibition of muscle insulin signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of GLUT-4 trafficking in insulin-responsive cells.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the translocation of GLUT4-containing vesicles to the plasma membrane in response to insulin.
understanding the mechanisms of insulin action in muscle and fat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Rab10 is a key regulator of GLUT4 translocation and insulin-stimulated adipocyte glucose uptake, and that disruption of Rab10-dependent insulin signaling causes hepatic insulin resistance.
adipose Rab10-dependent GLUT4 translocation is a major determinant of insulin sensitivity.
disruption of adipose Rab10-dependent insulin signaling causes hepatic insulin resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rab10 is required for insulin signaling in adipose cells and is necessary for the full effect of the insulin signal on glucose uptake.
Rab10-dependent insulin signaling is required for the full effect of the hormone on adipose GLUT4 translocation and glucose uptake.
disruption of adipose Rab10-dependent insulin signaling causes hepatic insulin resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the full effect insulin has on glucose uptake is the integration of Rab10-dependent (and Rab10-independent) pathways.
the full effect on glucose uptake of insulin is the integration of Rab10-dependent GLUT4 trafficking and Rab10-independent signaling.
the full effect on insulin action in adipose is the integrated effect on both the Rab10-dependent and independent pathway.
